main_text.l: portet omnibus iis, qui spatia in curriculo
philosophico conficere feliciter satagunt. Sat-
agentia enim in hoc cursu est frustra, nisi præ-
cognitorum sax[?] præferatur: quum, teste phi-
losopho, omnis disciplina sit è præcognitis, &
veluti anticipatis. Denique hæc ipsa materia
fructu est insignis, idq; quatuor modis. Prin-
cipiò enim occurrunt, quæ modò dixi, prin-
cipia, regulæ illæ veri & boni, quæ ostendunt
discrimen turpis & honesti, quæ docent, quid
facias, quid fugias,
——— quid fiet utile, quid
non; quæ denique existunt basis disciplinarum, &
quia disciplinarum, etiam universæ vitæ.
Tolle mihi hæc talia principia, sive cognitio-
nis illa sint, sive actionis, labascet protinus vita
nostra, & quia labascet, ne vita quidem, sed
ipsissima mors, id est, caligo & horror, erit.
Tolle notitias illas primas, protinus Cyclopica
ingenia, facient

l.i: Candida de nigris, & de candentibus atra,

main_text.l: hoc est, cœlum terræ miscebunt; adeoque eve-
niet, quod Homerus de lignis male compos-
itis cecinit, ut videamus
Πολλά τ᾽ ἀνύντα, καὶ πάντα, πάραντά τε δόγμα[?]τ᾽ ἐλθεῖν.
Has igitur vitæ nostræ magistras oportet
nos paulo altius cum animis nostris repeter-
e & reputare, si velimus illas nobis esse normas.
Qualis enim, amabo, norma, quam non nōris?
Nulla certè. Normâ vel circino Geodæta non
uteretur, nisi utriusque naturam
& utilitatem

page.notes: The word after "nisi præcognitorum" is printed as "fax", which is not a Latin word; it is probably "sit" with the long s misread, so it is marked [?]. The dash at the start of the last line is printed as a long rule and is copied as a dash. The page is cut off after this line. The Greek line is set in a smaller type with accents; the word after "δόγμα" is doubtful. "nōris" carries a mark over the o that may be a circumflex or macron. A small printed mark stands to the left of the catchword and was not read as text. The narrow strip of letters at the far right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and was left out.
